label: Founded populated pasts from state-causal finitism and the precedence bridge
meaning: Prices horn H2 of the initial-state view with causal finitism. An unfounded populated moment t starts a strictly descending sequence of moments (dependent choice); its members below t are pairwise distinct because the strict temporal order is irreflexive and transitive, and by the precedence bridge each is a causal ancestor of the state at t; so t has infinitely many distinct ancestors, against finite distinct ancestry. No no-loops premise is needed. The two premises are independent and both needed (controls 1 and 2): finitism alone is satisfied by causally idle earlier states, and the bridge alone by an endless past in which every earlier state causes every later one. Both premises are OPEN; the bridge is the explicit step from mere temporal precedence to causation. No premise is established.
